questions.question_text: Solve the following equation: 12 - x = 4
Solve the following equation: 9x - 4 = 6x + 8
Solve the following equation: \frac{12}{x} + 5 = 9
Solve 6x^2 - 5x + 1 = 0.
Use your answer to part (b)(i) to solve 6\sin^2 x - 5\sin x + 1 = 0 for 0^\circ \leqslant x \leqslant 90^\circ.
Write down the mode.
Find the range.
Find the median.
Find the inter-quartile range.
Calculate an estimate of the mean.
Give a reason why your answer to part (e) is an estimate.
Two of these students are chosen at random. Find the probability that the highest mark of these students is 2.
On the diagram sketch the graph of y = f(x), for -90 \leqslant x \leqslant 90, where f(x) = 1 - 2\sin(2x - 10)^\circ.
Write down the co-ordinates of the x-intercepts.
Write down the co-ordinates of the local maximum.
The graph of y = -\frac{x}{60} intersects the graph of y = 1 - 2\sin(2x - 10)^\circ three times. Find the value of the x co-ordinate at each point of intersection.
Find the co-ordinates of point A, given that ABCD is a rectangle and the equation of the line AB is 4x + 3y = 24.
Find the co-ordinates of point B, given that ABCD is a rectangle and the equation of the line AB is 4x + 3y = 24.
Find the co-ordinates of the midpoint of AB.
Rearrange the equation 4x + 3y = 24 to make y the subject.
Find the equation of the line BC. Give your answer in the form y = mx + c.
Find the co-ordinates of point C.
Find the co-ordinates of point D.
Calculate the number of fish in the lake in January 2019, given that the number of fish decreases by 4% each year and in January 2018 there are 30000 fish.
Calculate the number of fish in the lake in January 2029.
Calculate the number of fish in the lake in January 2017.
Find the last year in which there were at least 50000 fish in the lake.

Philip runs a fishing business and he works 50 weeks every year. In 2018, he catches 800kg of fish in each of these weeks. He sells all the fish he catches at a price of $3.50 for each kilogram. Calculate the total amount he receives in 2018.
For each of the 50 weeks, Philip’s business costs $2240 to run. Calculate his profit as a percentage of $2240.

In 2019, Philip’s business costs 8% more to run than in 2018. The selling price of fish decreases by 10%. Find the amount of fish, in kilograms, Philip will need to catch each week to keep the percentage profit found in part (c)(ii) the same.
Reflect triangle A in the line x = -2. Label the image B.
Rotate triangle A through 180° about (-2, -1). Label the image C.
Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle C onto triangle B.
Enlarge triangle A with centre of enlargement (1, 2) and scale factor 2. Label the image D.
Find an expression for the nth term for the sequence: 80, 77, 74, 71, ...
Find an expression for the nth term for the sequence: 128, 64, 32, 16, ...
The nth term of a sequence is n^2 - 1. Find the first four terms of this sequence.
The nth term of a sequence is |n - 3|. Find the first four terms of this sequence.
The nth term of a sequence is n^2 + n + 41. Find the first three terms of this sequence.
Show that when n = 41 the number in this sequence is not prime.
Complete the statement. Angle OAT = ... because ...
DT = OC. Find angle ABC.
On the diagram, sketch the graph of y = f(x) where f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 4x + 1 for -3 \leqslant x \leqslant 5.
Write down the co-ordinates of the local minimum.
Find the range of values of k so that f(x) = k has only one solution.
g(x) = 3x^2 - 6x - 4 for -3 \leqslant x \leqslant 5. The graph of y = f(x) intersects the graph of y = g(x) twice. Solve f(x) > g(x).
Find an expression, in terms of a and/or c, for \vec{AC}.
Find an expression, in terms of a and/or c, for \vec{BC}.
Find an expression, in terms of a and/or c, for \vec{BD}, giving your answer in its simplest form.
Use your answer to part (a)(iii) to explain why \vec{OA} and \vec{BD} are parallel.
Explain why triangle OAX and triangle BDX are similar.
Find an expression, in terms of a and c, for \vec{AD}.
Find an expression, in terms of a and c, for \vec{XD}, giving your answer in its simplest form.
Find the ratio area AXO : area BXD.
Show that angle BAC = 36.0°, correct to 1 decimal place, given that triangle ABC has sides 8.6 cm and 9.3 cm and area = 23.5 cm^2.
Use the cosine rule to find BC.
All the angles in triangle ABC are acute. Use the sine rule to find the largest angle in the triangle ABC.
